While the confidence intervals encompass a wide range of plausible outcomes, certain high-impact, low-probability events could push the actual values beyond these boundaries. Conversely, a severe economic recession, major geopolitical instability, a large-scale natural disaster, significant adverse regulatory changes, or a sudden, dramatic shift in consumer behavior could trigger a decline far below our 1-month lower bound of 537.14. These "black swan" events, by their nature, are difficult to predict and incorporate into standard probabilistic forecasts, representing distinct risks to the accuracy of our stated intervals.
